ARCS kitMolecule 55sound-bite

Sound Bite

Put one real quote at a time in the hero, typed out fast, with who said it, so social proof reads in a glance without a wall of testimonials.

States

Anatomy

#PartType roleToken (CSS variable)
1Rail2px cyan rule on the left, the quote's only framecyan
2QuoteDisplay face at headline size; the untyped rest is laid out but transparent, so typing never moves the pagetext, --ds-font-display
3CaretA cyan block after the typed text while typing; no blinkcyan
4AttributionMono, sentence case (caps on a long label fail the all-caps rule): name in text, role and company in text-secondary--ds-font-mono
5ControlsPrev, the count, Next and Pause, each 44px; shown only once the script runssurface, border

Usage

Use it when

  • The hero needs social proof and the quotes are real, attributed and already public (a recommendation, a client line).
  • Two to five short quotes, each under about 30 words.

Do not use it when

  • Never invent or paraphrase a quote, and never use one without the person's name and role.
  • Do not use it for a single long testimonial; use 31 Callout or plain text.
  • Do not stack several of them on one page.

Data it reads

FieldTypeRequiredNote
bites[]{text, name, role}yestext verbatim from its public source; name and role exactly as published.
source{label, href}noWhere the quotes are published, shown at the right of the controls.

Access

  • Without the script every quote shows as a list; the script hides all but one with visibility and aria-hidden, so the box keeps the tallest quote's height and nothing below jumps.
  • The full text is in the DOM while typing (the rest is transparent, not missing), so a screen reader reads the whole quote; the count is a polite live region.
  • prefers-reduced-motion turns off typing and the timer; Pause, hover and focus all hold it.
